glossdef.p: The motherboard, or mainboard, is the main circuit board inside your computer which connects together all of the other parts. There are many manufacturers, with the most popular being ASUS, ASRock, GIGABYTE, and MSI.

Your motherboard’s processor socket type must match the CPU and fit inside your case. An Intel chip will not fit in a motherboard designed for AMD chips, and you must also match the socket type. For instance, an Intel i5-12500 processor needs an LGA 1700 socket on the motherboard.

Your board will also need enough slots for everything you want to install, although that is rarely a concern. Also, take note of the form factor of your motherboard, such as ATX or mini-ITX. This determines the limits on size and power for the motherboard. For a first-time builder I would recommend a micro-ATX or ATX form factor for their flexibility.
